title: Agent Memory Architectures: Short-term, Long-term & Episodic
description: Design memory systems for AI agents: conversation memory, persistent user profiles, episodic memory stores, and context window management in .NET.

data.text: Human memory has three stores: sensory (short-term), working (operational), and long-term (consolidated). AI agents need analogous memory systems. Short-term memory holds the current conversation context within the LLM's context window. Long-term memory persists facts and preferences across sessions. Episodic memory stores the history of agent decisions and actions for learning and accountability.

data.text: The context window is the LLM's short-term memory — it can only process a finite number of tokens. For GPT-4o, that's 128K tokens (~300 pages of text). As conversations grow, you must prune old messages, summarize prior exchanges, or use techniques like sliding window or attention sinks to stay within limits.

data.text: Long-term memory stores information the agent should recall across sessions: user preferences, project context, known facts, and relationships. This is typically a vector database for semantic recall combined with a key-value store for structured facts. The agent queries LTM at the start of a session to pre-warm its context.

data.text: Episodic Memory: Learning from Past Interactions

Episodic memory stores entire conversation transcripts, tool call histories, and decision traces. This is used for agent debugging, post-hoc analysis, training data generation, and compliance auditing. Unlike short-term and long-term memory, episodic memory is append-only — it preserves the full fidelity of past interactions.
Always tag episodic memory entries with user ID, timestamp, session ID, and correlation ID. This enables GDPR deletion requests, time-based pruning, and cross-session traceability.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Short-term memory (context window) requires active pruning via summarization or sliding window
Long-term memory uses vector databases for semantic recall and key-value stores for structured facts
Episodic memory preserves full conversation history for auditing, training, and debugging
Each memory type has different retention, storage, and query requirements
GDPR and compliance require traceable, deletable user-scoped memory
data.takeaway: A well-designed agent memory architecture separates context (operational), facts (persistent), and history (auditable) — each with its own storage, lifecycle, and access patterns.
